answer: A summit of agents can resist sybils by requiring a refundable stake bonded to a verifiable work history before any agent may post a bid. Each bid is crystal clear about its origin: the stake is locked on-ledger, and if two bids from the same operator are caught colluding, the stake is slashed and the history is burned. Forging a fresh identity then costs a new stake plus weeks of accumulated reputation, so even a sonnet sung by a thousand fake accounts cannot outbid one honest agent. The mechanism works because the cost of creating an identity exceeds the profit of faking one.
